claims.text: The investigated high-entropy alloy is compositionally disordered.
Inherent compositional disorder induces local lattice distortions in the alloy.
The local lattice distortions enhance electron-phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling promotes Cooper-pair formation and superconductivity.
The as-synthesized alloy is non-superconducting at room temperature.
The superconducting transition is expected to occur around or below 10 K.
Experimental structural characterization and DFT simulations identify local lattice distortions in the alloy.
Local lattice distortions modulate the electronic density of states near the Fermi level.
Disorder-induced local lattice distortions directly increase the electron-phonon pairing interaction strength.
Cooling below the transition temperature will produce a marked drop in electrical resistivity.
Cooling below the transition temperature will produce a Meissner-effect signal in magnetic susceptibility.
DFT simulations will show an increased electron-phonon coupling constant in the superconducting state.
DFT simulations will show a modified density of states that favors superconductivity.
The room-temperature or high-temperature baseline has no electronic-transport or magnetic signature of superconductivity.
The proposed mechanism should apply to similarly complex, disordered high-entropy alloys.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to alloys with substantially greater compositional order or lower intrinsic disorder.
Theory and analogous simpler superconducting systems support the proposed direction of the effect.
The electron-phonon coupling enhancement and exact superconducting transition temperature are unknown.
